$comment:
Documents that do NOT survive carveToHtml -> htmlToCarve(roundtrip) -> carveToHtml unchanged, and the ones the import refuses outright. Each diverging entry holds the HTML the document re-renders to, compared byte for byte, so a recorded loss that changes shape fails too. Data, not a skip list: tests/roundtrip.mjs fails on a divergence that is NOT here, on an entry here that has started surviving, and on a recorded output that has moved. `unsettled` names the documents a SECOND import changes again; every other document reaches a fixed point after one pass. Regenerate with UPDATE_ROUNDTRIP_LEDGER=1 node --stack-size=4000 tests/roundtrip.mjs, and say in the commit message what moved. The recurring classes, so a reviewer can size a diff without reading 500 names: inline whitespace collapses through the DOM (a double space, a soft line break); boolean attributes come back spelled out (disabled -> disabled=""); a rendered construct comes back as the raw HTML that produced it rather than as its Carve spelling (task-list checkboxes); and per-cell table alignment has no home in the Carve table syntax the writer emits, so it is dropped. Added when the engine pin moved to carve-rs 9cf16d05: an attribute-less div unwraps to its content on import (carve-rs#1269, ruled on carve#1578), so a bare ::: box does not come back and neither does anything that depended on it wrapping; and a figure div's bracket label comes back as a labelled paragraph, which renders as a figure group rather than a figure div (carve-rs#1310, one document). The f2fbb24c pin adds five known divergences: generated endnotes are not reconstructed from rendered HTML, an authored heading ID remains explicit, and three container/list layout distinctions have no equivalent in the imported HTML tree. The 4bb927af pin REMOVES ten and adds none. A task item comes back a task item instead of as the raw checkbox HTML that rendered it (carve-rs#1366, with the content-column readings in carve-rs#1364 and carve-rs#1374), which clears eight documents including the one whose marker carries an attribute block; and a grouping label keeps its div fence (carve-rs#1322), which clears two. Nothing was added for the heading-id round trip that carve-rs#1324 broke: carve-rs#1355 reads an id's position and value to tell a generated one from an authored one, so roundtrip mode stopped re-emitting a derived id as authored and the two documents it cost never needed an entry. The f5e2a888 pin adds 22 measured divergences, mostly authored heading identity and source-only spelling that rendered HTML cannot reconstruct, removes two stale entries, and records one malformed-Unicode refusal. Released carve-rs 0.1.4 at 2e9c43f2 adds 33 corpus cases whose source-only fence, column, continuation, caption, and invisible-definition distinctions are absent from rendered HTML and therefore cannot be reconstructed; its importer improvements simultaneously clear 97 stale divergence entries and the malformed-Unicode refusal. The 7219b3df checked-render work adds one caption-separator case: a tab in an image caption's marker separator is layout, so HTML import cannot reconstruct it from the rendered caption text. Released carve-rs 0.1.5 at 56cb3536 adds 42 source-layout corpus cases (categories 439-458: a colon followed only by whitespace, a raw block's passed-through attributes, marker folding between an item's base and content column, degraded and unterminated comment fences in list items and at a container's column 0, a definition's reachable column under a host, and a wrapped attribute block's boundary) whose fence, column, continuation, and attribute-order distinctions are absent from rendered HTML and cannot be reconstructed; it clears no prior entry, and its lone nesting-cap refusal is unchanged. The 9a0c421d pin moves two rows, and NEITHER is an engine defect. It ADDS 461-a-column-0-line-after-a-description-hosted-note-is-a-document-sibling-4: the HTML importer reads a soft break as layout and collapses it to a space, which is what HTML white-space processing says it is (PART 11 section 7), so `
  • nested tail
    • ` imports as `
  • nested tail
    • `. It is general rather than description- or list-specific - `

    a` newline `b

    ` imports as `a b` in every host and all three modes - and it is not a regression: the same divergence is present at ec5ac508, 9a0c421d and 8e2736bc. It is the 239th member of the whitespace-run class this ledger already rules expected, 238 of which were already here.
